segments.text: A news poll says: fifty-two percent of voters support a new metro line, plus or minus three percent.
segments.caption: A news poll says: 52% of voters support a new metro line, plus or minus 3%.

segments.text: What does that plus or minus three actually mean? It's a confidence interval. Let's make it simple.
segments.caption: What does that plus or minus 3 actually mean? It's a confidence interval. Let's make it simple.

segments.text: Pollsters can't ask everyone, so they ask a sample of one thousand people.
segments.caption: Pollsters can't ask everyone, so they ask a sample of 1,000 people.

segments.text: Another thousand might give fifty-one, or fifty-four.
segments.caption: Another 1,000 might give 51, or 54.

segments.text: So one number alone can mislead.
segments.caption: So one number alone can mislead.

segments.text: Think of fishing.
segments.caption: Think of fishing.

segments.text: A single number is like a spear: you'll probably miss.
segments.caption: A single number is like a spear: you'll probably miss.

segments.text: A range is like a net: far more likely to catch the fish.
segments.caption: A range is like a net: far more likely to catch the fish.

segments.text: A confidence interval is that net.
segments.caption: A confidence interval is that net.

segments.text: Here's the definition you can use in an interview.
segments.caption: Here's the definition you can use in an interview.

segments.text: A confidence interval is a range of values, calculated from a sample, that is likely to contain the true population value.
segments.caption: A confidence interval is a range of values, calculated from a sample, that is likely to contain the true population value.

segments.text: And the confidence level, like ninety-five percent, tells how reliable that method is.
segments.caption: And the confidence level, like 95%, tells how reliable that method is.

segments.text: Example one: the poll.
segments.caption: Example one: the poll.

segments.text: Fifty-two, plus or minus three, means a range from forty-nine to fifty-five percent.
segments.caption: 52, plus or minus 3, means a range from 49 to 55%.

segments.text: The true support among all voters is likely somewhere in there.
segments.caption: The true support among all voters is likely somewhere in there.

segments.text: Example two: averages.
segments.caption: Example two: averages.

segments.text: A food app checks one hundred orders. The average delivery time is thirty-two minutes.
segments.caption: A food app checks 100 orders. The average delivery time is 32 minutes.

segments.text: Its ninety-five percent confidence interval is thirty to thirty-four minutes.
segments.caption: Its 95% confidence interval is 30 to 34 minutes.

segments.text: The recipe is always the same: estimate, plus or minus a margin of error.
segments.caption: The recipe is always the same: estimate, plus or minus a margin of error.

segments.text: For ninety-five percent, the margin is about two standard errors.
segments.caption: For 95%, the margin is about two standard errors.

segments.text: And the standard error is the spread, divided by the square root of the sample size.
segments.caption: And the standard error is the spread, divided by the square root of the sample size.

segments.text: Here: ten divided by ten is one. So the margin is two.
segments.caption: Here: 10 divided by 10 is 1. So the margin is 2.

segments.text: Now, the part most people get wrong.
segments.caption: Now, the part most people get wrong.

segments.text: Ninety-five percent does not mean a ninety-five percent chance that this one range is right.
segments.caption: 95% does not mean a 95% chance that this one range is right.

segments.text: It means: repeat the survey one hundred times, and about ninety-five of the ranges will catch the true value.
segments.caption: It means: repeat the survey 100 times, and about 95 of the ranges will catch the true value.

segments.text: Two things change the width.
segments.caption: Two things change the width.

segments.text: More data makes it narrower: four times the sample halves the margin.
segments.caption: More data makes it narrower: four times the sample halves the margin.

segments.text: More confidence makes it wider: to be ninety-nine percent sure, you need a bigger net.
segments.caption: More confidence makes it wider: to be 99% sure, you need a bigger net.

segments.text: So remember: a confidence interval is an estimate, plus or minus a margin of error.
segments.caption: So remember: a confidence interval is an estimate, plus or minus a margin of error.

segments.text: A range that likely contains the true value.
segments.caption: A range that likely contains the true value.

segments.text: Quick quiz!
segments.caption: Quick quiz!

segments.text: Average sleep is seven hours, with a ninety-five percent confidence interval of six and a half to seven and a half hours.
segments.caption: Average sleep is 7 hours, with a 95% confidence interval of 6.5 to 7.5 hours.

segments.text: Does that mean ninety-five percent of people sleep that long?
segments.caption: Does that mean 95% of people sleep that long?

segments.text: No!
segments.caption: No!

segments.text: It's a range for the average, not for individual people. Lots of people sleep less, or more.
segments.caption: It's a range for the average, not for individual people. Lots of people sleep less, or more.
